newsitem.title: USA: Giant Cement sees record 1997 production.
newsitem.headline: Giant Cement sees record 1997 production.

text.p: Giant Cement Holding Inc said Monday it anticipates record production levels for the balance of 1997 as a result of first quarter maintenance and capital improvements.

At the same time, the company expects production cost per ton for all of 1997 to be slightly below 1996 costs and foresses selling out its production for the year, said Gary Pechota, chairman, president and chief executive officer.
The company made the forecast as it reported revenues for the first quarter of 1997 at $24.4 million, up 17 percent from $20.8 million in the comparable quarter in 1996.
It said first quarter net income increased 26 percent to $1.2 million, or $0.13 per share, compared with $986,000, or $0.10 per share, a year earlier.
Pechota said sales volume rose 9.8 percent during the quarter because of good weather and strong demand in the Middle Atlantic region as well as continued strength in the South Atlantic region.

He said that favorable supply/demand fundamentals should result in the realization of the $4 per ton general price increase, implemented April 1, 1997, by its Keystone Cement and Giant Cement units in the Mid-Atlantic and South Atlantic regions, respectively.
